reconcile.note: Every inter-candidate disagreement below was settled by DIRECT CODE VERIFICATION by the reconciler rather than by vote — grounded beats confident. The specific files/lines read to settle each dispute are recorded in disputes_resolved[].

synthesis: Org admins in Scout Bird's Eye — the same Vue/Pinia app the driver PWA runs, in adminMode — can select a hit but cannot disposition it. The disposition control in the shared MapShell.vue is gated only on the selected hit carrying a scan_id, not on driver mode, so this is a backend-only change. Three gaps block it: the two admin hit-payload builders on ClarityScoutBirdsEyeController omit scan_id (and disposition); the scout/org-map/api route group has no POST route so the save 405s; and the driver's disposition controller is kit-scoped (kit_id === user->kit_id), which would 404 for an admin on every scan they did not personally drive. The outcome is parity: an admin sets a disposition through the existing UI, it persists to Postgres and syncs to ClickHouse, is audit-attributed to the admin, and the hit optimistically keeps/hides exactly like the driver flow — with org tenancy enforced on the write and zero driver-behavior change.

scope.summary: Add scan_id AND disposition to both admin Bird's Eye hit payloads; add a throttled POST scout/org-map/api/scan/disposition route inside the existing auth + ClarityScoutAdminMiddleware group; add a new thin org-scoped ClarityScoutBirdsEyeDispositionController that reuses the existing ScoutScanDispositionRequest and mirrors the DRIVER controller's tenancy-404 and reason-normalization patterns (NOT DispositionController's, which would introduce two defects).

proposed_changes.change: In the hits() payload map, add 'scan_id' => $hit->scan_id and 'disposition' => $hit->disposition.
proposed_changes.reason: scan_id is the sole gate on MapShell.vue's disposition control (MapShell.vue:79). disposition is what seeds the control from the saved value on re-open (MapShell.vue:236 `selectedDisposition.value = hit?.disposition ?? ''`); the driver payload carries it with an explicit DEV-2059 F1 comment, so omitting it would leave an admin's already-set disposition rendering as a blank placeholder — a real parity break, not cosmetic.

proposed_changes.change: In the recentHits() payload map, add 'scan_id' => $hit->scan_id and 'disposition' => $hit->disposition as DISTINCT keys alongside the existing 'id' => $hit->id.
proposed_changes.reason: CAUTION (verified): this map already emits 'id' => $hit->id, which is the ClickHouse Hit ROW id, NOT the scan. scan_id must be added as a separate key — renaming or reusing 'id' would silently post the wrong identifier. Beyond rendering, scan_id here is REQUIRED for AC-2: dashboard.js routes recentHits through mapStore().applyHiddenScanIdsFilter and map.js's KEEP-patch matches on h.scan_id === scanId, so with scan_id undefined the optimistic keep/hide is a no-op on this surface.

proposed_changes.change: NEW single-invoke controller. (a) Validate with the EXISTING App\Http\Requests\ScoutScanDispositionRequest (no new FormRequest). (b) Resolve the scan OUTSIDE any try/catch: Scan::query()->where('id', $request->input('scan_id'))->forOrg((int) auth()->user()->org_id, withSharedKits: Feature::active(FeatureEnum::SHARED_KITS->slug()))->firstOrFail(). (c) Normalize reason exactly as the driver does: $reason = $request->input('disposition') === DispositionEnum::INVALID_SCAN->value ? ($request->input('reason') ?? 'other') : 'other'. (d) $scan->updateDisposition(disposition:, user: $request->user(), reason: $reason) inside a try/catch returning 500 on failure. (e) Analytics::track('disposition-saved', $request->user(), ['scan_id'=>..., 'disposition'=>..., 'reason'=>$reason, 'from_scout'=>true], page: ScoutAnalyticsPage::BirdsEye->value) in its OWN try/catch so a tracking failure never blocks the save. [DECIDED human:Dalton 2026-08-03 — additive page tag, from_scout boolean NOT widened.] Return response(status: 200).
proposed_changes.reason: A dedicated controller is REQUIRED for correctness, not just for tidy analytics. Reusing DispositionController would import TWO verified defects: (1) it wraps the tenancy lookup in a try/catch that swallows ModelNotFoundException into a 500 — its own test pins 500 for a cross-org scan — whereas the driver controller deliberately keeps the lookup outside the try/catch, its comment stating tenancy failures 'must be unambiguous'; (2) it forwards $request->input('reason') raw, and map.js OMITS the reason key for every non-Invalid-Scan disposition (`if (reason) { payload.reason = reason; }`), so reason arrives null — and Scan::updateDisposition's guard is `if ($reason !== 'other')`, which null satisfies, spuriously creating a human-review ScanValidation row on EVERY Accessible / New Hit / Moving / Inaccessible admin save. DispositionController's existing web caller masks this by always sending 'other' client-side.
proposed_changes.ref: app/Http/Controllers/DispositionController.php:16-48; app/Http/Controllers/Api/ClarityScoutScanDispositionController.php:19-43 (both comments verified); app/Models/Scan.php:513-535 (the `$reason !== 'other'` guard, verified); resources/js/clarity-scout/stores/map.js:833-836 (the omission, verified)

proposed_changes.change: Inside the scout/org-map Route::prefix('api') group, grouped with the explicit routes and ABOVE the GET-only {any} JSON-404 catch-all: Route::post('scan/disposition', ClarityScoutBirdsEyeDispositionController::class)->middleware('throttle:30,1');
proposed_changes.reason: The group is GET-only today, so the save cannot land. throttle:30,1 mirrors the driver Scout disposition route exactly, which is the ticket's stated parity target. Registering above the catch-all keeps it consistent with the group's existing ordering (the catch-all is GET-only so it would not intercept a POST regardless).

proposed_changes.change: Extend recentHits() assertions to pin scan_id + disposition, and ADD a first-ever test for hits() pinning the same two keys.
proposed_changes.reason: hits() has NO dedicated test today, so without a new one the map-marker half of this change ships unpinned. The existing seedHit() helper already defaults scan_id, keeping this cheap.

proposed_changes.change: NEW test class (Postgres-only, NOT RequiresClickhouse) mirroring DispositionControllerTest + ClarityScoutScanDispositionControllerTest conventions.
proposed_changes.reason: Pins the org-scoped write, the 404-not-500 tenancy behavior, the reason-normalization fix, admin audit attribution, and the middleware gating.

acceptance_criteria.item: In Birds Eye, selecting a hit shows the disposition control and an admin can set a disposition; it persists (meta.disposition + ClickHouse sync) and is attributed to the admin in the activity log.
acceptance_criteria.reason: Delivered by the payload additions + the new org-scoped controller. Scan::updateDisposition already writes meta.disposition, dispatches SyncDispositionToClickhouse, and logs activity('Disposition')->causedBy($user) unconditionally — since $request->user() is the admin, attribution is correct with zero extra code. Note: full parity requires the disposition field too, or the control renders blank on re-open.

acceptance_criteria.item: The hit is optimistically kept/removed per KEEP_VISIBLE_DISPOSITIONS, matching driver behavior, and does not reappear on the next poll (within the suppression TTL).
acceptance_criteria.reason: The store logic is already adminMode-agnostic, but this AC is NOT free: it depends on scan_id reaching the recentHits payload, because both the KEEP-patch (h.scan_id === scanId) and the dashboard store's applyHiddenScanIdsFilter key on scan_id. Verified KEEP_VISIBLE_DISPOSITIONS = ['New Hit','Accessible'] and HIDDEN_SCAN_TTL_MS = 3 minutes.

acceptance_criteria.item: Org scoping holds: an admin can only disposition hits within their own org's scope (incl. the Staging-Live decision above); driver disposition behavior is unchanged.
acceptance_criteria.reason: Scan::forOrg is kit-ownership scoped, the same axis as the read side's forKitOrg, so the write set is a superset of the display set — no visible hit can 404 on save (see Q3). Driver behavior is unchanged because no driver file is touched.

acceptance_criteria.item: A non-Invalid-Scan disposition set from Birds Eye must NOT create a ScanValidation human-review row.
acceptance_criteria.reason: Derived from verified code, not from the ticket. This is the defect the naive 'reuse DispositionController' reading would introduce; the driver path already guards it. Without this AC the feature would silently pollute the human-review queue on nearly every admin save.

acceptance_criteria.item: A cross-org scan must return a clean 404, not a 500.
acceptance_criteria.reason: Derived from the driver controller's explicit design comment ('tenancy failures here must be unambiguous'). DispositionController's swallow-to-500 is pinned by its own test, so reusing it would make an authorization failure indistinguishable from a server error.

acceptance_criteria.item: The disposition-saved analytics event from Bird's Eye carries from_scout=true AND page='clarity-scout-birds-eye', leaving the existing from_scout semantics unchanged.
acceptance_criteria.reason: Settled at the Phase-2 gate (human:Dalton 2026-08-03, option a). Makes admin-vs-driver dispositions separable in analytics without changing the meaning of an existing field.

questions.q: Analytics discriminator: the disposition-saved event currently carries a single boolean from_scout (false = web admin panel, true = driver Scout PWA). An admin dispositioning from Bird's Eye is a THIRD source that does not fit the boolean. Should it (a) send from_scout=true and additionally tag page: ScoutAnalyticsPage::BirdsEye (an unused enum case 'clarity-scout-birds-eye' already exists in the codebase with no callers, apparently reserved for this), (b) send from_scout=true with no extra tag and stay indistinguishable from a driver save, or (c) widen the discriminator to a string/source field (a small change to existing analytics semantics)?
questions.answer: (a) Send from_scout=true AND additionally tag page: ScoutAnalyticsPage::BirdsEye->value ('clarity-scout-birds-eye'). Purely additive — no existing analytics series changes meaning, admin-vs-driver stays separable via the page tag, and it activates an enum case already reserved for this surface. The from_scout boolean is NOT widened.
questions.materiality: material — data semantics of an existing analytics series; option (c) changes an established field's meaning. Flagged needs-human by 3 of 4 prep passes.
questions.conservative_default_if_yolo: (a) from_scout=true + page: ScoutAnalyticsPage::BirdsEye — purely additive, breaks no existing series, and uses an enum case already reserved.

questions.q: Enum breadth: should admins in Bird's Eye be restricted to the 5 driver-facing dispositions (New Hit / Accessible / Moving / Inaccessible / Invalid Scan), or eventually be allowed the wider admin set (Valid / Reviewed / Invalid)? For THIS ticket the code settles the implementation — MapShell.vue's DISPOSITION_OPTIONS hardcodes exactly the 5 with no adminMode branch, so under 'no frontend changes' the UI can never send more, and reusing ScoutScanDispositionRequest enforces that server-side. But the ticket explicitly asks to 'decide intentionally', and there IS a counter-precedent: BulkDispositionAction already exposes the FULL DispositionEnum to admins on the Filament Hits resource. Confirm restricting to the 5 (and treat widening as a separate ticket)?
questions.answer: Restrict to the 5 driver-facing values (New Hit / Accessible / Moving / Inaccessible / Invalid Scan), enforced server-side by reusing the existing ScoutScanDispositionRequest. True parity with the driver; no frontend change. Widening to the full DispositionEnum is explicitly a SEPARATE future ticket (it needs a MapShell.vue adminMode branch to be reachable at all).
questions.materiality: material — AC ambiguity the ticket itself flagged for an intentional decision. Note the implementation does not block on it: the recommended build restricts to the 5, and widening later would require a frontend change anyway.
questions.conservative_default_if_yolo: Restrict to the 5 driver values; widening is a separate ticket requiring a UI change.

questions.q: Which controller should back the route — reuse DispositionController, or a thin dedicated ClarityScoutBirdsEyeDispositionController?
questions.answer: Dedicated thin controller. Unanimous across all 4 prep passes, and settled by code for a correctness reason stronger than the ticket's own analytics/throttle rationale: reusing DispositionController would import both the swallow-tenancy-into-500 behavior and the raw-reason passthrough that spuriously creates ScanValidation rows against map.js's payload shape.

questions.q: Staging-Live scope subtlety (DEV-2053): does the read side's forKitOrg diverge from the write side's forOrg, leaving hits visible but undispositionable?
questions.answer: NO divergence — the ticket's concern rests on a naming collision across two different models. App\Clickhouse\Models\Hit::scopeForOrg filters hotlist_org_id (the DEV-2053 ambiguity) but the hit READ path never uses it; hits()/recentHits() use scopeForKitOrg (kit_org_id) and additionally pre-filter kit_ids to the org's own kits. The disposition WRITE happens on the Postgres Scan model, whose scopeForOrg has no hotlist concept at all — verified at app/Models/Scan.php:435-443 it resolves Kit::getKits($org_id, withShared)->pluck('id') then whereIntegerInRaw('kit_id', $kitIds), i.e. kit-ownership, the SAME axis as kit_org_id. So the write set is a superset of the display set (identical, plus shared kits when SHARED_KITS is active) and an admin can disposition every hit they can see, Direct and Staging-Live alike. Independently reached by all 4 passes and then verified directly in the code by the reconciler. An existing test already documents the Staging-Live case (a divergent hotlist_org_id with the same kit_org_id).

questions.q: Should the new POST route be throttled, and at what rate?
questions.answer: Yes — throttle:30,1. Settled by code against a candidate that claimed no sibling disposition endpoint is throttled: routes/api.php:62 verifiably registers the DRIVER disposition route with ->middleware('throttle:30,1'). Since this ticket's stated goal is parity with that driver endpoint, matching its throttle is the precedent-following choice. (The web DispositionController route at routes/web.php:89 is indeed unthrottled, which is the likely source of the confusion.)

questions.q: Is a CSRF exemption needed for the new POST?
questions.answer: No. The scout/org-map group lives in routes/web.php under the default web middleware (session + CSRF), and lib/fetch.js's authHeaders() already attaches X-CSRF-TOKEN in adminMode.

questions.q: Does a new FormRequest subclass need to be created for the admin path?
questions.answer: No. Verified ScoutScanDispositionRequest is generic — authorize() is just auth()->check() with no kit/driver binding, and rules() already restricts disposition to DispositionEnum::formOptions(missedOpportunity: false), exactly the 5 values MapShell offers. Reuse it as-is; the fast pass's proposed ScoutBirdsEyeScanDispositionRequest would be pure duplication.

plan_sketch.intent: Seed a Live hit (clarity.hits_hot, dated relative to now()) for an org's kit plus its underlying Postgres Scan. As that org's admin, GET /scout/org-map/api/map/hits and /dashboard/recent-hits and assert scan_id AND disposition are present. POST /scout/org-map/api/scan/disposition with that scan_id + 'Accessible'; assert 200, scans_metadata.meta.disposition updated, an activity_log row with log_name Disposition causedBy the admin, and SyncDispositionToClickhouse dispatched.

In a browser as an org admin, open Bird's Eye, select a hit, confirm the disposition control renders with the same 5 options a driver sees, save one, then RE-OPEN the same hit and confirm the control shows the saved value rather than a blank placeholder (this is what the disposition payload field buys).

POST a HIDE disposition (Moving or Inaccessible) and confirm the hit disappears from BOTH /map/hits and /dashboard/recent-hits and does not reappear on a re-poll inside the 3-minute TTL; POST a KEEP disposition (Accessible) and confirm the hit stays with its disposition reflected.

Seed a Staging-Live hit whose hotlist_org_id belongs to a DIFFERENT org while kit_org_id stays the admin's org; confirm it is visible AND dispositionable (200, not 404) — the concrete regression test for the resolved Q3. Separately, attempt a scan on another org's kit entirely and assert 404 (not 500).
POST a non-Invalid-Scan disposition with NO reason key and assert NO scan_validations row is created; then POST Invalid Scan with a real reason and assert one IS created.
Assert the cross-org attempt returns 404 specifically, distinguishing authorization failure from a 500.

qa_hint.seed_scenario: One org with an admin user (RoleEnum::ADMIN, CLARITY_SCOUT active) and at least one Scout-enrolled kit. Seed a Postgres Scan on that kit plus a matching clarity.hits_hot row (hit_type Live, hotlist_id -> an Open clarity.hotlist row, kit_org_id = the org, scan_id -> the Postgres Scan).
